analysis:
The PR changes SSDPrefixCache.retireIndexedEntries (patch hunk around lines 1791-1802) to call a new SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices helper. Each slice acquires removalLock separately and re-checks hasSafeRoot and ownsEvictionRoot, then calls SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.remove, which goes through the epoch barrier. The PR adds tests for the slicing behavior. The helper's source file is not in the supplied units, so I could not read removeInSlices itself. The tests at SSDOwnedEntryRetirementTests.swift lines 105-151 show the intended contract: slices of 16, a refused (nil) slice stops the batch, earlier removals are kept, and an empty batch still makes one ownership-checked call.

Security-relevant reading (T-041, TB-007, A-001): the change shortens lock holds and does not touch the crypto, HMAC lookup tags, TTL values, salt scoping or the KEK purge. The ownership and safe-root check now happens per slice, so losing ownership mid-batch halts further deletion. That is fail-closed and stops the cache from deleting under a successor's root. The tests cover the case where the epoch record is invalidated after the first slice.

TTL sweep behavior (sweepExpiredEntries, lines 1849-1856) is functionally unchanged. A batch can now be partially retired when ownership is lost. The index is only updated for files actually removed (result.removed). externalChange still triggers reconcileExternalRemovals. Remaining files stay indexed until later reconciliation. Expired entries that survive a refused batch are retried on the next sweep, so TTL enforcement is slightly delayed but not bypassed.

The scanOnDisk and settleDurableDonation code in the supplied excerpt is unchanged context: symlink and safe-URL checks, binding validation, and a durable-ready receipt that re-decrypts. I saw no regression.

Open question for the next pass: the SSDOwnedEntryRetirement.removeInSlices implementation, including its slice size, nil handling and result merging, was not visible in these units and should be confirmed.
